response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan AS timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.n) AS total_distinct_orders, AVG(g.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM g, a WHERE g.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: The ratio rebrate/feerate is computed per fee row and then averaged within each time-in-force group; rows with NULL rebrate or feerate are ignored, and a feerate of 0 gives NULL in SQLite, so such rows are ignored too.
Orders with a NULL timespan, if any, form their own group and count toward the cross-group average, since GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group.
Distinct orders are counted by distinct orders.recordvault among orders that have at least one matching fee.
